apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- Android: regenerate the PGO profile on the GS span source
- GS/HW: a target takes the destination-alpha loop only after more than 64 such draws in a frame
- GS/Vulkan: the Adreno 613's destination-alpha loop leaves only the targets it reads uncompressed
- GS/Vulkan: on the Adreno 613 destination-alpha draws read the target in the pass
- GS: with draw buffering off, the draw's environment is copied once
- GS: sprite pair layouts enter the two-pass kick kernel, autoflush included
- GS/SW: build only the colour table entry a row's span reads
- GS/HW: copy road kernels read the texture a block at a time and write the frame a block row at a time
- GS/TC: a block grid per target in place of the dirty rectangle lists
- Android: Auto hides the on-screen controls for a connected pad only on a handheld
- Android: ask again whether a gamepad is attached when the activity is created
- GS/HW: compute this draw's cover test before the CPU sprite verdict

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261104...afd93842f99be9ea8d5730a9d20f1222f1b40cd8
